children: European shares were subdued on Monday as rising oil prices following fresh U.S.-Iran attacks stoked inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the European Central Bank could raise interest rates later this week.

Energy stocks (.SXEP) advanced 1.2%, tracking higher oil prices. Brent crude futures
rose more than $1 a barrel as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption.
Higher oil prices have fuelled inflation concerns, strengthening the case for further policy tightening.

The ECB is widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points on Thursday, while U.S. CPI data later this week comes into focus after a strong jobs report boosted expectations of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve this month.
Investors will also monitor second-quarter euro zone economic data due later in the day. Trading volumes could be lighter than usual with U.S. stock markets closed for a public holiday.
